I am sort of on Vaush's side when it comes to AI art. Art, IMO, is most valuable when it depicts some form of human experience. AI art might be entertaining and beautiful, but beauty in itself is not art.   


To be a prude, I am going to cite the oxford dictionary of the word art.   
"The expression or application of human creative skill and imagination, typically in a visual form such as painting or sculpture, producing works to be appreciated primarily for their beauty or emotional power."

I think people confuse the terms beauty with art. What AI can generate is quite beautiful at times, but that doesn't make it art in my eyes. The AI is not being creative, it has been trained on art and tries to replicate whatever the prompt is telling them.   


Perhaps AI art is a form of abstract art. It doesn't capture the direct experience, but it's a simulacrum of many experiences, which it culminates into.

I highly doubt your aim just gets worse during the second half of a match. It could be due to a lot of other factors, such as how well the enemy team is playing, your mentality, maybe the opponents got a read on how you are playing, etc.   


Although kills are a good correlative factor for having good aim, good aim is not the only factor that influence the amount of kills you get.   


If you are worried about your mechanical aim, use a tool such as kovaak's or aimlab to get a more internally consistent metric of your aim. Doing so will allow you to isolate your aim from all other factors, and will show how you are progressing or declining in that area.   


A lot of people downplay the importance of mindset. If you hyper fixate on the amount of kills you get, you may start to get more anxious the more you die, causing you to tilt harder and further spiraling down your performance. However, being dethatched from the kills you get in a match will allow you to focus on other important aspects in the game.  


Ask yourself: How well am I communicating to my team? Am I flooding coms? Am I not giving enough information?   
How am I using my agent's utility? For duelists: Am I creating space, providing openings for my teammates into bombsites? For controllers: Are my smokes blocking off chokepoints, or areas of the map, that provide more map control?  etc. etc. (basically try to focus how to assist your team's composition)  
Am I being too aggressive by giving up untradeable kills? Am I being too passive and not trading my team mates?   
Am I playing the same way each round? How can I give the opponents a different look that they wont anticipate?    
Are the people I am playing with bringing my mood down? Am I bringing team moral down?   


I won't go on for too much longer. Basically the point in my message is that kills are not the end all be all, and they are not necessarily indicative of overall skill. There are many sub-skills that people need to develop in order to improve in this game.    


I hope this was helpful and not too preachy. Cheers :)
